FAQ
Identify The Body Before The Appointments
The zeros identify size, while 42 identifies the appointment style. Use the
Martin model-number guide
to compare the measured lower bout with the Concert 0, Grand Concert 00 and Auditorium 000 families. Familiar nominal widths are a
Count the frets to the body and photograph the complete outline square-on. A 12-fret body has different proportions from a later 1
Measure scale from the nut’s string-bearing edge to the center of the twelfth fret and double that distance. The saddle includes c
small-body Martin history
explains the familiar 24.9-inch 000 and 25.4-inch OM references. George Gruhn’s examination of a
records a 25.4-inch scale. That is a documented early 000 configuration. A long scale on such a guitar does not turn it into an OM
On a phone, swipe sideways to read all three table columns.
Three Sizes, Separate Identification Questions
Model
Starting Point
Follow-Up
Small Concert body, often early 12-fret construction
Establish period materials and intended stringing
Grand Concert body and its original neck joint
Check bridge generation, stringing and any special-order features
Auditorium body, with scarce early and later 14-fret groups
Measure scale, nut width and internal construction before assigning a group
Style 40, 42 And 45
Trace The Pearl Around The Fingerboard Extension
2012 Martin 000-42: abalone top border and rosette. The photograph illustrates trim placement on a modern example.
2012 Martin 000-42: rosewood back with a decorative center strip and plain perimeter binding.
Follow the pearl along the top edge, around the soundhole and around the end of the fingerboard. Robert Corwin’s
documented Style 40 and 42 instruments
show the distinction: Style 42 continues pearl around the fingerboard extension, while Style 40 omits that connecting decoration.
Style 45 adds pearl decoration around the back and sides. A decorative wood center strip on a Style 42 back isn’t pearl trim. The
; its date and specifications belong to that later instrument.
Look for interrupted borders, replacement binding, uneven channels and finish changes where pearl meets the top. These observation
Headstock lettering and snowflake markers require period context. Early Style 42 guitars can have plain fingerboards; Corwin’s arc
A History With Gaps
Separate Early Orders From Later 000-42 Production
Nineteenth Century
Early Pearl Instruments
The 0-42 belongs to an older Style 42 tradition. Its materials, neck construction, finish and stringing need the
early Martin inspection approach
. A missing modern-style model stamp is not enough to reject a nineteenth-century guitar.
1918 And The 1920s
Scarce Early 000 Examples
Corwin’s
top-border research
documents a 1918 000-42 with fan bracing for Hawaiian steel-string use. That exceptional instrument demonstrates why bracing and i
1930s Through 1943
Early Orders And Later 14-Fret Production
The vintage price chart separates rare early entries, 1938, the two 1939 neck-width groups and the final wartime years. Treat thos
Later Production
Modern Standard, Signature And Authentic Models
The 2012 guitar shown here belongs to modern production. Read every suffix and the serial year before using specifications or pric
Neck, Top And Hardware
Inspect A Prewar 000-42 As A Complete Instrument
A documented
, provides a historical reference for the model’s Brazilian rosewood body and red-spruce top. That record describes a specific gui
For a claimed 1939 example, measure the nut width and photograph the neck profile. The chart distinguishes the earlier 1 3/4-inch
Inside, record the X intersection, brace profiles, glue joints and bridge plate. X position and scalloping are different observati
prewar Martin construction guide
explains the wider chronology; use it alongside model-specific evidence. Later carving can imitate a scalloped profile while remov
Tuners need photographs from the front and rear. Look for extra holes, enlarged post holes, disturbed finish and outlines from ear
Grand Concert Details
Check The 00-42 On Its Own Timeline
The 00-42 retains its own relationship among body, neck and bridge. Greig Hutton’s factory-record account of
documents a particular instrument with a wide 1 7/8-inch nut, ebony belly bridge, scalloped X-bracing, T-frets and steel T-bar rei
Hutton also records Grover G-97 tuners, a headstock decal and a rear headstock stamp on that example. Compare the complete hardwar
For earlier 00-42s, distinguish the pyramid-bridge period from later steel-string construction. The value chart’s two groups overl
The
Style 42 price chart
also identifies a solitary 1973 00-42 entry. It is a separate later example, not a continuous postwar production band. Recent 00-4
Concert-Size Pearl Guitars
Read Early 0-42 Materials And Stamps In Context
1930 Martin 0-21 from Joe’s archive: a labeled 12-fret Concert-body comparison. It is not a Style 42.
2012 Martin 000-42: complete modern 14-fret instrument, shown to distinguish recent production from vintage originals.
Martin’s serial-number sequence began in 1898. An earlier 0-42 can therefore lack a serial number. Corwin documents an 1894 exampl
The adjacent 1930 0-21 photograph supplies body context only. Its simpler trim does not illustrate Style 42 ornament, and its cons
The
Martin serial and model reference
helps interpret dated stamps. Photograph the neck block, center strip, rear headstock and any penciled date without sanding or cle
1921 000-42 examination
describes the serial-only neck-block marking typical from 1898 through late 1930. A guitar from that period can have a serial but
Changed bridges, refinishing and neck repairs deserve particular attention on these early bodies. A replacement part may have been
Read The Serial Year And Suffix
Recognize A Modern Martin With Historical Styling
2012 Martin 000-42: pearl headstock lettering and modern hardware. Match these details to the actual production year.
2012 Martin 000-42: visible model and serial, with part of the maker’s stamp covered.
Martin’s
000-42 Authentic 1939 specifications
describe a modern recreation with a 24.9-inch scale, rearward scalloped X-bracing, Madagascar rosewood and a VTS-treated Adirondac
A recent Standard Series 000-42, an Authentic model and a signature edition can have different woods, neck shapes, appointments an
Read Joe’s pictured block in stages. The model line says 000-42, and the serial below reads 1615472. Martin’s
official serial table
ends 2011 at 1555767 and 2012 at 1656742. The photographed number falls in 2012, agreeing with this guitar’s archive record.
The dark pad covers part of the maker’s stamp above those readable lines. That is a separate observation from the date calculation
Evidence Before A Conclusion
Spot Counterfeits And Altered Martin Identities
Counterfeit D-45 comparison from Joe’s fake-Martin guide. This is not a 0, 00 or 000 guitar.
1950 Martin 000-28: oversized replacement bridge documented in Joe’s listing.
The counterfeit stamp photograph is from Joe’s fake D-45 example, a different body and style. Look at the thin, serif-style letter
fake Martin examination
. Compare how those markings were formed with the machine-stamped characters in the pictured 2012 block. The guitars are from diff
A faint impression, one uneven letter or an obstructed logo would not establish a counterfeit. On the suspect example, the typogra
Compare the logo, body outline, neck joint, bridge position, inlay layout, internal construction and stamps. Look for mismatches b
Also consider altered real guitars: added pearl, replaced tops, changed necks and modified stamps can create a misleading model id
The 1950 000-28 bridge photograph shows a disclosed oversized replacement on a different model. It illustrates the kind of repair
finish inspection guide
helps distinguish evidence of touch-up, overspray and refinishing. Neither an attractive surface nor convincing aged hardware reso

The companion chart starts with
The Official Vintage Guitar Price Guide, 2026 edition
: page 277 for 0-42, page 280 for 00-42 and page 284 for 000-42. Each row receives one fixed editorial reduction of 11 to 15 perce
The 1930/1932 entry needs particular care. Page 284 groups those years under a 14-fret description, while Gruhn’s early-production
An annual range cannot capture every exceptional example or later change in demand. The original case, finish, wood, structural re
A Practical Photo Set
Document The Guitar Before Repair Or Purchase
Capture Identity
Send square front and back views, both headstock faces, the complete model and serial, and the neck-to-body joint. Add body, scale
Show Structure And Changes
Include bridge height, remaining saddle, action, cracks, binding and accessible interior details. Have a repairer photograph areas
Keep The History Attached
Include the case, labels, repair invoices and any earlier photographs. Separate documented work from an owner’s recollection and i
Send The Evidence
Ask Joe About Your Style 42
I’m happy to help identify a Martin 000-42, 00-42 or 0-42 and discuss its condition. Pawn brokers are welcome to send photographs

No. Early examples can have plain fingerboards. Compare the claimed period with documented instruments before treating a missing i

A lookup can help date a number. It can’t establish whether the number belongs to the guitar, whether the model is correctly descr

Once the model, period and repairs are documented, use the
